easy.def: A spot where something is or happens.
examples: This is a quiet place.
Put it back in its place.
The park is my favorite place.

more.def: A particular spot, area, or building where something is or happens.
examples: The library is a quiet place to read.
Penguins live in some of the coldest places on Earth.
Find a good place to set up the tent.

easy.def: To put something somewhere with care.
examples: Place the cup here.
She placed the book on the shelf.
I placed my hat down.

more.def: To put something in a particular spot, usually with care.
examples: Please place your lunch box on the shelf.
He placed the candles on the cake one by one.
The artist placed each tile carefully on the floor.

related.def: To move something out of its place.

easy.def: Where something is put.
examples: The placement of the desk.
Check the placement.
Good placement helps.

more.def: The act of putting something in a certain place, or the position where it is placed.
examples: The placement of the lamp makes the room feel cozy.
The teacher checked the placement of each student's desk.
Careful placement of the flowers made the garden pretty.

easy.def: A sickness that spreads very fast.
examples: A plague spread through the city long ago.
The plague was bad.
Many people got sick in the plague.

more.def: A deadly disease that spreads quickly through many people.
examples: In the story, a plague forced the villagers to leave.
Doctors worked to stop the plague.
The story is about a town hit by a plague.

easy.def: A pattern of crossing stripes of different colors.
examples: My shirt is plaid.
A plaid skirt.
The blanket is plaid.

more.def: A pattern of crossing stripes of different colors, or the cloth that has this pattern.
examples: She wore a red plaid skirt to school.
The blanket was made of soft plaid wool.
My dad has a plaid shirt for camping.

easy.def: Simple, with nothing added.
examples: I like plain pasta.
The room is plain.
She wore a plain dress.

more.def: Simple and ordinary, without decoration or anything extra.
examples: He wore a plain white shirt.
The cake was plain, with no frosting.
The plain wooden table had no paint at all.

easy.def: A large, flat piece of land.
examples: Buffalo walked on the plain.
The farm is on a plain.
We crossed the wide plain.

more.def: A large area of flat land with few trees.
examples: Herds of bison once roamed the great plains.
The train rolled across the flat plain.
Wheat grows well on the wide plain.

easy.def: An idea of what you will do.
examples: I have a plan.
What is the plan?
Our plan is to swim.

more.def: A set of ideas about how to do something or what to do later.
examples: Our plan is to hike to the lake and have lunch there.
The builder drew a plan of the new treehouse.
Her plan for the science fair was to grow beans.

easy.def: To think about what you will do.
examples: We plan a trip.
She planned a party.
I plan to read.

more.def: To decide ahead of time what you will do and how to do it.
examples: We are planning a surprise party for my grandmother.
He planned his route before the bike ride.
I plan to finish my book this week.

easy.def: A machine with wings that flies.
examples: The plane is in the sky.
We took a plane.
A plane landed.

more.def: A machine with wings and engines that flies in the air carrying people and goods.
examples: The plane took off from the airport.
We flew on a plane to see Grandpa.
A small plane circled over the field.

easy.def: A big, round thing in space that goes around a star.
examples: Earth is the planet we live on.
Mars is a red planet.
Our planet has land and sea.

more.def: A large, round object in space that travels around a star such as the sun.
examples: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system.
Saturn is the planet with bright rings.
We must take care of our planet.

easy.def: A long, flat board of wood.
examples: We walked on a plank.
A plank of wood.
The plank was long.

more.def: A long, flat piece of wood that is thick and used for floors, bridges or building.
examples: We laid a plank across the stream to make a bridge.
The floor of the old barn was made of wide wooden planks.
Dad cut the plank into pieces to make shelves.

easy.def: A person or a book that helps you plan.
examples: She is a party planner.
I write in my planner.
The planner has dates.

more.def: A person who plans things, or a notebook where you write down plans and dates.
examples: My aunt is a party planner and organizes birthdays.
I write my homework in my planner every day.
The city planner drew a map of the new park.

easy.def: A living thing that grows in the ground.
examples: The plant needs water.
Trees are plants.
I water the plant.

more.def: A living thing that grows in soil or water and makes its own food from light.
examples: The plant grew toward the window.
Trees, grass and flowers are plants.
Cactus plants store water in their stems.

easy.def: To put seeds in the ground.
examples: We plant seeds.
She planted a flower.
Dad planted a tree.

more.def: To put seeds or young growing things in the ground so they will grow.
examples: We plant tomatoes every spring.
She planted a row of beans.
Dad planted a tree in the backyard.

easy.def: A building where things are made.
examples: The car plant is big.
He works at a plant.
The plant makes toys.

more.def: A large building where things are made or power is produced.
examples: The power plant makes electricity.
My uncle works at a car plant.
The plant makes thousands of tires a day.

easy.def: A very large farm in a warm place.
examples: We saw a coffee plantation.
The plantation grows sugar.
The plantation is big.

more.def: A very large farm in a warm place where crops such as cotton, tea or coffee are grown.
examples: We toured a coffee plantation on our trip.
Workers picked tea leaves on the plantation.
In the past, many plantations used enslaved people to work the fields.

easy.def: A flat sign on a wall with words on it.
examples: A plaque is on the wall.
The plaque has a name.
I read the plaque.

more.def: A flat piece of metal or stone with writing on it, put on a wall to remember someone; also the sticky film that grows on teeth.
examples: A bronze plaque on the wall names the people who built the school.
The dentist said that brushing every day removes plaque from my teeth.
The plaque beside the statue tells about the town's history.

easy.def: A thick wet mix that dries hard on walls.
examples: The wall is covered in plaster.
Plaster dried on the ceiling.
A crack is in the plaster.

more.def: A thick paste that dries hard, used to cover walls and ceilings, or to hold a broken arm still.
examples: Workers spread smooth plaster over the walls of the new room.
A crack ran across the old plaster ceiling.
The doctor put a plaster cast on the broken arm.

easy.def: To cover a wall with a thick wet mix.
examples: Workers plaster the wall.
She plastered the poster on the wall.
He plastered the hole.

more.def: To spread a thick paste over something, or to cover a surface with lots of things.
examples: The workers plastered the new walls and let them dry.
He plastered the walls of his room with posters.
She plastered the crack in the ceiling before painting it.

easy.def: A light, hard material that is made in factories.
examples: The cup is plastic.
Toys are made of plastic.
Plastic floats.

more.def: A light, strong material made in factories and used to make many things.
examples: Many toys are made of plastic.
The bottle is plastic, so it will not break.
Recycling helps keep plastic out of the sea.

easy.def: A flat dish that you eat from.
examples: Put the food on the plate.
My plate is empty.
The plate is round.

more.def: A flat dish used for serving and eating food.
examples: She put a sandwich on her plate.
The plate fell and broke.
Please set the plates on the table.

easy.def: A raised, flat place.
examples: The speaker stood on the platform.
The train platform is crowded.
The platform is high.

more.def: A flat, raised area where people stand, such as a stage or train station area.
examples: The speaker stood on a platform.
We waited on the train platform.
The diver jumped from the high platform.

easy.def: A large flat plate for serving food.
examples: The platter has cookies.
A platter of fruit.
She carried a platter.

more.def: A large, flat dish used for serving food.
examples: A platter of cookies sat on the table.
She carried a platter of fruit to the party.
Grandpa put the turkey on a big platter.

easy.def: A strange animal with a duck-like bill that lays eggs.
examples: A platypus swam in the river.
The platypus has a bill like a duck.
We saw a platypus.

more.def: A furry Australian animal with a flat bill and webbed feet that lays eggs and swims in streams.
examples: A platypus uses its flat bill to find food in the mud.
The platypus is one of the few mammals that lays eggs.
Platypuses swim in rivers and streams in Australia.

easy.def: To do things for fun.
examples: I play with my dog.
The kids play outside.
We played a game.

more.def: To take part in a game or activity for fun.
examples: The children played tag in the yard after lunch.
My sister plays soccer on Saturdays.
We played a board game when it rained.

easy.def: To make music with an instrument.
examples: I play the drum.
She plays the piano.
He played a song.

more.def: To make music with an instrument, or to make a recording start.
examples: My brother plays the trumpet in the school band.
Please play that song again.
She played a tune on the violin for her grandfather.

easy.def: A story that people act out on a stage.
examples: We saw a play.
Our class has a play.
The play was funny.

more.def: A story written to be acted out on a stage.
examples: Our class put on a play about the three little pigs.
The play had a happy ending and the audience clapped.
She had the lead part in the school play.

easy.def: Playing a sound or video that was recorded.
examples: Press playback.
The playback was clear.
Playback of the video.

more.def: The act of playing a recorded sound or video again so that you can hear or see it.
examples: Press the playback button to hear the recording again.
The playback of the video showed the winning goal.
The singer listened to the playback of her voice.

easy.def: A person who plays a game.
examples: The player kicked the ball.
Each player has a card.
She is a good player.

more.def: A person who takes part in a game or sport.
examples: The soccer player scored a goal.
Each player picks a card.
The team has ten players.

easy.def: Liking to play and have fun.
examples: The puppy is playful.
She has a playful smile.
A playful kitten chased a string.

more.def: Full of fun and ready to play.
examples: The playful puppy chased its tail.
She gave a playful push to her sister.
A playful kitten pounced on the string.

easy.def: A place outside where children play.
examples: We play on the playground.
The playground has a slide.
The playground is full.

more.def: An outdoor area with swings, slides and other things for children to play on.
examples: We play on the playground at recess.
The playground has a slide and swings.
The park has a new playground.

easy.def: A friend you play with.
examples: She is my playmate.
A new playmate.
The playmates laughed.

more.def: A friend, especially a young child, who you play with.
examples: My cousin is my favorite playmate.
The puppy found a new playmate in the garden.
The two playmates built a fort out of blankets.

easy.def: A game played to decide who wins.
examples: We won the playoff.
The playoff is on Friday.
A playoff game.

more.def: An extra game or a series of games played after the regular season to decide who is the champion.
examples: Our team made it into the playoffs after the regular season ended.
The playoff game was tied, so there was extra time.
She cheered loudly during the playoff.

easy.def: A person who writes plays.
examples: The playwright wrote a play.
A famous playwright.
The playwright watched the show.

more.def: A person who writes plays for the theater.
examples: The playwright wrote a play about a talking tree.
A famous playwright lived in England long ago.
The playwright watched the first show from the back row.

easy.def: An open square in a town.
examples: We met at the plaza.
The plaza has a fountain.
Kids played in the plaza.

more.def: A large open square in a city or town where people gather.
examples: We met at the plaza near the fountain.
The plaza was full of people.
Musicians played in the plaza.

easy.def: A strong request for help.
examples: He made a plea for help.
The plea was loud.
They heard her plea.

more.def: A strong, serious request for something.
examples: She made a plea for help.
The town's plea for food was heard.
He ignored the child's plea.

easy.def: To beg.
examples: I plead with you.
She pleaded to go.
The child pleaded for a cookie.

more.def: To ask for something in a strong, serious way.
examples: She pleaded with her parents to let her go.
The children pleaded for one more story.
He pleaded for help.

easy.def: Nice to see, hear or be with.
examples: We had a pleasant day.
The weather is pleasant.
She has a pleasant voice.

more.def: Giving you a feeling of enjoyment, or friendly and kind.
examples: We spent a pleasant afternoon by the lake.
The weather was warm and pleasant.
Our new neighbor is very pleasant and always says hello.

easy.def: A polite word you say when you ask for something.
examples: Please pass the milk.
Can I have a cookie, please?
Please help me.

more.def: A polite word used when asking for something or telling someone to do something.
examples: Please close the door quietly when you leave.
Could I have some more water, please?
Please be careful with the glass.

easy.def: Happy about something.
examples: I was pleased with my picture.
Mom looked pleased.
The dog seems pleased to see us.

more.def: Feeling glad and satisfied because something went well.
examples: The coach was pleased with how hard the team worked.
She was pleased to get an A on her report.
The farmer was pleased when the rain finally came.

easy.def: Nice and enjoyable.
examples: A pleasing smell.
A pleasing song.
The room is pleasing.

more.def: Giving pleasure or enjoyment, so that you like it.
examples: The bakery had a pleasing smell of fresh bread.
The painting is pleasing to the eye.
The singer has a pleasing voice.

easy.def: A happy feeling.
examples: Reading gives me pleasure.
It is a pleasure to meet you.
She smiled with pleasure.

more.def: A feeling of happiness or enjoyment.
examples: It was a pleasure to see you again.
Reading gives her great pleasure.
He splashed in the puddles with pleasure.

easy.def: A serious promise.
examples: I made a pledge.
We say the pledge.
Her pledge was to help.

more.def: A serious promise to do something.
examples: We say the Pledge of Allegiance at school.
She made a pledge to clean up the park.
He kept his pledge to help.

easy.def: To promise.
examples: I pledge to help.
She pledged ten dollars.
We pledged to be kind.

more.def: To make a serious promise to do or give something.
examples: I pledge to do my best.
She pledged ten dollars to the fund.
The scouts pledged to help others.

easy.def: More than enough.
examples: We have plenty of food.
There is plenty of time.
There is plenty of room.

more.def: A large amount, as much as you need or more.
examples: There is plenty of food for everyone.
We have plenty of time before the bus.
The pond has plenty of fish.

easy.def: A tool for holding or bending things.
examples: Dad used pliers.
The pliers are in the box.
I held the nail with pliers.

more.def: A tool with two handles used for gripping, bending or cutting wire.
examples: Dad used pliers to bend the wire.
She held the nail with pliers.
The pliers hung on a hook in the shed.

easy.def: To fall with a soft splash.
examples: The frog will plop in the pond.
A pebble plopped into the water.
He plopped on the couch.

more.def: To fall or drop with a soft sound, or to sit down heavily.
examples: The frog plopped into the pond.
She plopped down on the couch after school.
A drop of paint plopped on the floor.

easy.def: The main events in a story.
examples: The plot is exciting.
The story has a good plot.
I like the plot.

more.def: The series of events that make up a story.
examples: The plot of the story is about a lost dog.
The movie had an exciting plot.
The plot has a surprise at the end.

easy.def: A small piece of land.
examples: We planted a vegetable plot.
The plot is by the fence.
The garden plot is small.

more.def: A small area of ground, such as one for a garden.
examples: We planted tomatoes in the garden plot.
The family bought a plot of land.
The class has a small plot for flowers.

easy.def: A big tool for turning over soil.
examples: The farmer used a plow.
The plow is heavy.
A snow plow cleared the street.

more.def: A large farm tool that turns over the soil, or a machine that clears snow.
examples: The farmer used a plow to turn the soil.
The farmer's plow left neat rows in the field.
The horse pulled the plow.

easy.def: To dig up soil with a big tool.
examples: The farmer plows.
He plowed the field.
They plowed the fields.

more.def: To cut and turn over soil or snow using a large blade.
examples: The farmer plowed the field in spring.
The truck plowed the snow.
They plowed the road after the storm.

easy.def: To pull something off or out quickly.
examples: I pluck a flower.
She plucked an apple.
He plucked a feather.

more.def: To pull something out or off with a quick tug.
examples: I plucked a ripe apple from the tree.
She plucked a feather from her hat.
The farmer plucked the weeds from between the rows.

easy.def: To pull the strings of an instrument with your fingers.
examples: She plucks the guitar strings.
He plucked the harp.
I plucked a string.

more.def: To pull and let go of the strings of a guitar or harp with your fingers to make a sound.
examples: She plucked the guitar strings softly.
He plucked the harp and the room filled with music.
I plucked a string on the violin instead of using the bow.

easy.def: A piece that you push into a wall to get electricity.
examples: Put the plug in the wall.
The plug is loose.
Pull out the plug.

more.def: A small piece with metal pins that you push into a wall to bring electricity.
examples: I put the plug into the wall.
The lamp's plug fell out.
Pull the plug out of the socket.

easy.def: Something that stops up a hole.
examples: Put a plug in the sink.
The plug stopped the leak.
A plug is in the drain.

more.def: Something that you push into a hole to close it.
examples: He put a plug in the sink and filled it with water.
A plug stopped the leak in the pipe.
The plug in the bathtub held the water in.

easy.def: A soft, round purple fruit with a pit.
examples: I ate a plum.
The plum is sweet.
A plum fell off the tree.

more.def: A round, soft, juicy fruit with smooth skin and one hard seed inside.
examples: I bit into a juicy purple plum.
A plum tree grows behind our barn.
She made plum jam from the ripe fruit.

easy.def: Straight up and down.
examples: The wall is plumb.
A plumb line.
The post is plumb.

more.def: Exactly straight up and down, as a wall should be.
examples: The builder checked that the wall was plumb with a string and a weight.
The plumb line hung straight down.
The post was not plumb, so he fixed it.

easy.def: A person who fixes pipes.
examples: The plumber fixed the sink.
A plumber came.
The plumber has tools.

more.def: A person whose job is to put in and fix water pipes and sinks.
examples: The plumber fixed the leaking sink.
A plumber came to unblock the drain.
The plumber carried a heavy wrench.

easy.def: The pipes that bring water into a building and take it away.
examples: The plumbing in our house is old.
Water runs through the plumbing.
The plumbing made a funny noise.

more.def: The system of pipes, taps and drains that carries water into, through and out of a building.
examples: A leak in the plumbing flooded the kitchen floor.
The old school needed new plumbing in its bathrooms.
Cold weather can freeze the plumbing and make pipes crack.

easy.def: A big, soft feather.
examples: The bird has a long plume.
She wore a plume in her hat.
The plume was bright blue.

more.def: A large, soft feather, or something shaped like a feather.
examples: A tall white plume stood up from the knight's helmet.
A plume of smoke rose from the chimney into the sky.
The ostrich has soft plumes on its tail.

easy.def: To fall fast.
examples: The ball plummeted.
The stock plummeted.
The temperature plummeted.

more.def: To drop very quickly and suddenly.
examples: The rock plummeted into the canyon.
The temperature plummeted overnight.
The diver plummeted into the pool.

easy.def: Round and full.
examples: A plump hen.
A plump peach.
Plump cheeks.

more.def: Round, soft and full in shape.
examples: The plump little hen laid a brown egg.
I bit into a plump, juicy peach.
The baby has soft, plump cheeks.

easy.def: To jump or fall into something suddenly.
examples: I plunge into the pool.
The ball plunged into the water.
The diver plunged in.

more.def: To jump or fall suddenly into something, or to push something into something.
examples: I plunged into the cool pool.
The ball plunged into the lake with a splash.
He plunged his hands into the cold water to find his keys.

easy.def: A quick jump or fall into something.
examples: I took a plunge in the pool.
The plunge was cold.
The plunge was fun.

more.def: A sudden jump, dive or drop.
examples: We took a quick plunge in the cool lake.
The cliff made a steep plunge to the sea.
The diver made a plunge from the high board.

easy.def: Added to.
examples: Two plus two is four.
Three plus one is four.
Add five plus five.

more.def: Used when you add numbers together.
examples: Two plus three equals five.
Ten plus ten is twenty.
Add four plus six to get ten.

easy.def: And also.
examples: I need a pencil plus an eraser.
We saw lions plus tigers.
Buy milk plus bread.

more.def: And also, or in addition.
examples: Pack your swimsuit plus a towel.
We packed sandwiches, plus apples and juice.
She plays piano, plus she sings.
